title: Secret Dates in System Prompts Undermine Language Model Evaluation
key_facts: A new paper from researchers in Germany, Mexico and the USA, 'Dating the Model: Hidden Dates in System Prompts Affect LLM Evaluation', says the current date is automatically inserted into system prompts of frontier and many open-weight models.
Across 9 models, 6 datasets and four tasks, changing the date alters performance and reshuffles leaderboard rankings, more than batch size or numerical precision.
Performance varied by up to 6% on multiple-choice questions, 14% on mathematical reasoning and 7% on code generation.
GPT-5.1 accuracy fluctuated by up to 4% across three multiple-choice benchmarks over a week in December 2025, even with an empty system prompt and zero randomness.
Step-by-step reasoning made date sensitivity worse; five example answers cut average variation only from 2.52% to 2.27%.
Six different prompt wordings affected accuracy about as much as changing the date (0.78%).
The authors recommend removing the date or fixing and documenting it in tests.
quote_evidence: ‘Across 9 models, 6 datasets, and four tasks, this dynamic metadata alters model performance and reshuffles leaderboard rankings, surpassing the variance introduced by other system-level factors such as batch size or numerical precision.’
The researchers recommend removing the date from system prompts where possible, or fixing and documenting it, to ensure fair comparisons.
The effect was also identified in proprietary models, with GPT-5.1 showing accuracy fluctuations of up to 4% across three multiple-choice benchmarks during a week of testing in December 2025.
why_it_matters_hint: Benchmark scores used to rank AI models may shift with the day they were run.
event_date: Paper date not stated; GPT-5.1 testing was in December 2025; article published 9 Oct 2026
notes: New paper reported by Unite.AI; no outside review reported. Nine models tested are mostly small open models (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Phi, GPT-OSS) plus a separate GPT-5.1 check. Publication date of the paper not stated.
